MOBILE SIGNING AGENT DAY PICKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Ten offered signings, one notary: which should you take today?

Saying yes in the order the title companies text you, or taking the biggest fee first, fills the day with the wrong signings. Paste the offers — fee, print cost, appointment length, the window each borrower gives you and where they are — and get the exact set and order of signings with the highest profit for the day, the drive and idle time it implies, what each signing it turns down would need to pay, and what first-come booking leaves behind.

For mobile notaries, loan signing agents and other one-person appointment-driven field businesses. Nothing is uploaded: the text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device.

    Prefer a CLI?

    Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

    node cli.mjs plan signings.csv --start 08:00 --end 17:00 --hourly 35 --per-mile 0.70 --json
cat signings.csv | node cli.mjs plan - --speed 25

    Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: Which signings should a notary take in a day? Window and drive-time math.

    What's recognised

    InputHandling

    The plan is exact for the numbers you type (a search over every set and order, up to 14 signings). One agent and one home base; real traffic, one-way streets, a second notary, signings that must follow each other, customer cancellations and the value of a repeat customer are not modelled. Distance is straight-line miles times your circuity factor, not a routing service.

    Common questions

    Does it upload my signing list?

    No. The browser page works on the text you paste, in your own browser, and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.

    How is the best day found?

    The tool tries the signings as a search over which have been done and which was last, keeping every way to get there that is not both later and less profitable than another. That finds the exact best set and order for the numbers you give, and the tests compare it with trying every ordering of every subset.

    Why would it turn down a signing I would normally take?

    Because an agent can only be in one place. A signing that pays well but drives you across the map, or sits in a window that collides with two better signings, can cost more than the two it displaces. The tool says what the signing would need to pay to earn its place.

    Where do the costs come from?

    From your own books: fuel and wear per mile, and what an hour of your time costs you. They are your estimates, so treat the plan as a decision aid, not a forecast.

    Who is it for?

    Mobile notaries and loan signing agents choosing which offered signings to take today.

Closings are time-sensitive: do not use the plan to skip a signing a borrower is depending on. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use. It chooses between options using the numbers you supply; it is not a forecast of what will happen on the road.

    Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record. If a tool needs to survive, get cli.mjs and run it yourself.

    Everything runs in your browser. The text you paste is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (plan_run, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage and can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

which-signings-should-a-notary-take-in-a.text:
Mobile Signing Agent Day Picker · guide

Which signings should a mobile notary take in a day? Window and drive-time math

Short answer: pick the set and order of signings whose combined margin, after the drive between them, is highest and that all fit their appointment windows and get you home on time. You can be at one table at a time, so a good signing can be a bad choice if it displaces two better ones.

A worked day

Ten offered signings, one agent leaving at 08:00 and due back at 17:00, costing $35 an hour while driving or working and $0.70 a mile, driving 30 mph over roads 1.3 times the straight-line distance. Fees range from a $40 walk-in to a $200 reverse mortgage with a hospital-bed appointment.

  • Saying yes in the order the offers came in fits 4 signings and earns $196.25.
  • Highest fee first fits 2 signings and earns $70.77: it takes the $200 reverse mortgage, a long drive out with a 12:00 start, and that blocks most of the rest of the day.
  • The best day runs 5 signings, starting with the 09:00 refinance, and earns $265.20 over 62.3 miles, home at 16:36. That is $68.95 more than the best simple rule.

The reverse mortgage is turned down in the best day, and would earn a place only at about $254.65, so the fee to quote is that, not the $200 offered. The $55 apostille drop-off 17 miles out loses money even as the only signing and would need about $132.25.

What to feed it

  1. Hourly cost: what an hour of your time is worth to you, plus insurance, E&O and phone divided by hours actually worked, not hours paid.
  2. Per-mile cost: fuel plus tires and maintenance per mile driven.
  3. For each signing, the fee, your print and supply cost, the appointment length, the window the borrower or title company gives and the miles east and north from your home base.

Check any agreement with a title company or signing service first: some penalise declining or rescheduling, and a borrower waiting on a closing comes before any optimum.

Questions

How do I decide which loan signings to take?

Compare whole days, not single offers: for a set of signings in a given order, add what each pays after print and supply cost and appointment time, subtract the drive between them, and check every appointment window. The best day is the best such set and order. The picker finds it exactly for up to 14 signings.

Is taking the highest fee first a good rule?

Not reliably. The biggest fees often sit far from each other or in overlapping windows, so you drive and wait for them. On the worked day it earns $70.77 against $265.20 for the best day.

What should a signing pay to be worth a detour?

The picker prints, for each signing it turns down, the fee at which the best day would include it. That is the number to quote a far or awkward signing, or the number to give a title company that asks for a discount.

No warranty. This guide is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. It is not financial, tax, legal or business advice, and you are responsible for verifying its output, for the numbers you enter, and for any contract that obliges you to take a signing. The worked example is illustrative arithmetic, not a forecast.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. Do not use this as a system of record.
